author: bank_narrative
findings: Opening establishes Dairen/Dalian, Japanese administration, period and lending practice; qianzhuang is explained at first use.
Title promises an explanation of unequal access to credit. The narrative delivers through reputation, collateral and institutional backing; it does not promise a named individual telephone incident.
Four sections develop one credit chain. Grain documents, named firms and wartime permission thresholds give concrete content; no fictional borrower or unsupported transaction is inserted.
Named grain-trading firms are not assigned speculative transactions described generally in the source. Inclusive thresholds 50000/100000/30000 and eight surviving houses in 1944 match the extract.
Memoir attribution and overlapping witnesses remain explicit. Conditional cash-flow explanation is not represented as a particular historical crisis.
Photo caption identifies Yokohama Specie Bank and explicitly distinguishes the Longkou workplace. Existing provenance and uncertainty are retained.
Ending gives a concrete change in who could authorize a loan. No mandatory correction requested.
scope: Independent complete reader gate for Russian candidate and all metadata. Reviewer did not author or edit this version. Original loan contracts and Japanese legal acts were not independently examined.
